engines.name: 3.0L V6 turbo diesel (ML320 CDI, ML350 BlueTEC)
3.0L turbo inline-6 mild hybrid (GLE450, AMG GLE53)
4.0L twin-turbo V8 mild hybrid (GLE580, AMG GLE63)

issues.t: 7-speed automatic shifts harshly or goes into limp mode
issues.sym: Hard or clunky shifts, especially 1-2, 3-2 and 2-1 when cold, slipping, or the transmission getting stuck in one gear with a warning on the dash.
issues.why: The 7-speed automatic's internal control unit (often called the conductor plate) and its speed sensors fail with heat and age. Outdated shift software and worn internal parts cause rough shifting too.
issues.next: Have the transmission codes read. A software update fixes some cases; a failed conductor plate or valve body is replaced without removing the whole transmission. Change the fluid and filter on schedule.

issues.t: Transmission fluid leaks from the wiring connector
issues.sym: Reddish fluid dripping near the side of the transmission, oil wicking up the wiring harness, or erratic shifting and warning lights.
issues.why: The plug where the wiring enters the transmission is sealed with O-rings that harden and leak. Fluid can travel up the harness toward the control units.
issues.next: Have the connector and harness inspected. Updated connector seals are available; do it before fluid reaches the electronics.

issues.t: Airmatic air suspension sags and the compressor wears out
issues.sym: One corner or the whole SUV sits low after parking, a harsh or bouncy ride, the compressor running after shut-off, or an air suspension warning.
issues.why: On SUVs with Airmatic, the rubber air springs crack and leak with age. The compressor then runs much longer than designed and burns out.
issues.next: Have the system leak-tested. Replace a leaking strut early to save the compressor. Don't drive far if the SUV is sitting on its bump stops.

issues.t: Balance shaft gear wears and the check engine light comes on
issues.sym: Check engine light with camshaft and crankshaft position correlation codes, sometimes rough running. The engine may run fine at first.
issues.why: Early versions of the 3.5L V6 used a balance shaft (or idler) gear made of a soft metal that wears down, letting the cam timing drift. Mercedes later changed the part.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the build number checked by a Mercedes specialist. Fixing it means taking apart the front of the engine, so get a firm quote; ignoring it can lead to poor running and engine damage.

issues.t: Camshaft adjuster solenoids fail or leak oil
issues.sym: Check engine light, rough idle, weak acceleration, worse fuel economy, and sometimes oil seeping into the wiring connector.
issues.why: The magnets that control variable valve timing at the front of the engine wear out and can leak oil into their electrical plugs.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the solenoids inspected for oil. Replace leaking solenoids, and check the wiring harness for oil before it reaches the engine computer.

issues.t: Diesel oil cooler seals leak into the engine valley
issues.sym: A low oil warning, oil around the bell housing, or an oil-soaked belly pan and a burning smell.
issues.why: On the 3.0L diesel, the oil cooler sits in the V of the engine. Its gaskets harden with heat and oil runs down the back of the engine.
issues.next: Have the leak traced. The fix is labor-heavy because the intake must come off, so ask for related seals to be replaced at the same time.
issues.eng: 3.0L V6 turbo diesel (ML320 CDI, ML350 BlueTEC)

issues.t: Diesel emissions settlement repair and extended warranty
issues.sym: Usually no symptoms. Your SUV may still need its emissions fix, or you may be eligible for extended warranty coverage.
issues.why: BlueTEC diesels were sold with software that let emissions controls work less well on the road than in testing. A settlement requires a software update and sometimes new parts.
issues.next: Ask a Mercedes dealer to check your VIN for the emissions modification. Getting it done keeps the extended warranty on the affected parts.
issues.eng: 3.0L V6 turbo diesel (ML320 CDI, ML350 BlueTEC), 2.1L 4-cylinder turbo diesel (ML250 BlueTEC, GLE300d)

issues.t: Crankshaft pulley (harmonic balancer) separates
issues.sym: A wobble or chirp from the front of the engine, a thrown drive belt, then loss of charging, power steering or cooling.
issues.why: The rubber layer in the crankshaft pulley breaks down with age, letting the outer ring slip or come apart.
issues.next: Have the pulley checked at every service. Replace it at the first sign of wobble or cracking, before the belt comes off.

issues.t: Engine stalls when hot from a failing crankshaft sensor
issues.sym: The engine cuts out when warm and won't restart until it cools down, or it cranks without starting.
issues.why: The crankshaft position sensor tells the computer when to fire the spark plugs. When it fails with heat, the engine shuts off.
issues.next: Have it tested when the problem happens. A new sensor is a common fix.

issues.t: Catalytic converters break apart and rattle
issues.sym: A rattle from under the SUV, especially at idle or startup, or a check engine light for catalyst efficiency.
issues.why: The inside of the catalytic converters can crack and break loose with age and heat.
issues.next: Have the exhaust inspected. A rattling converter usually needs replacement, which is more work on this SUV because suspension parts may need to come off.

issues.t: Door lock actuators fail and lock buttons jump
issues.sym: Doors that won't lock or unlock with the remote, lock buttons moving up and down by themselves, or a door that won't open.
issues.why: The lock actuator inside the door latch wears out.
issues.next: Replace the latch assembly in the affected door.

issues.t: Power steering cooler hose can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: Power steering fluid leaking or spraying in the engine bay, a whining pump, or suddenly heavy steering.
issues.why: The clamp on the power steering fluid cooler hose may not grip tightly enough, so the hose can work off.
issues.next: Have the recall checked with your VIN. If steering gets heavy, slow down and have it towed.

issues.t: Cruise control may not switch off when braking (recall)
issues.sym: Cruise control stays engaged after you tap the brake, particularly if you pump the pedal.
issues.why: Under certain conditions, especially when the brake pedal needs unusually high force, the cruise control might not disengage.
issues.next: Don't use cruise control until a dealer confirms the recall is done. Turn it off with the switch, and brake firmly.

issues.t: Brake light warning from melted tail lamp sockets
issues.sym: A brake light bulb warning that keeps coming back even after new bulbs, or a brake light that works only some of the time.
issues.why: Heat from the bulb melts the socket in the tail lamp housing, causing a poor connection. Bad grounds cause the same message.
issues.next: Check the socket for melting or burning. Replacing the tail lamp housing or socket usually solves it.

issues.t: Power steering rack leaks and steering gets heavy
issues.sym: Puddles of power steering fluid, a whining pump, or steering that gets heavy, especially at moderate speeds.
issues.why: The steering rack's seals leak, and the system loses fluid and assist.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and look for leaks. A leaking rack is usually replaced; don't keep topping it up for long.

issues.t: Brake booster can corrode and fail (recall)
issues.sym: A hard or inconsistent brake pedal, longer stopping distances, or in rare cases little braking at all.
issues.why: Water can collect under a rubber sleeve on the brake booster and rust through its housing.
issues.next: This was a do-not-drive recall. Check your VIN right away and have it towed to a dealer if the recall is open.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning. In a crash the inflator can break apart and throw metal pieces.
issues.why: The driver's airbag inflator can build too much pressure when it deploys and rupture.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov and get the free airbag replacement right away.

issues.t: Fuel filter can leak (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell or drips near the fuel filter.
issues.why: On some 2011 models, a fuel filter O-ring wasn't lubricated during assembly, and on diesels the filter could leak around its heater. Either can let fuel escape.
issues.next: Have a dealer check the recalls on your VIN. Don't ignore a fuel smell.

issues.t: Water damages the fuel pump control unit and the engine stalls (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls while driving or is hard to start, and you may find water or corrosion in the spare tire well.
issues.why: Water can pool in the spare tire well, where the fuel pump control unit sits, and short it out.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 22V-955. Look in the spare tire well for water, and have the drains and seals checked.

issues.t: Rattle from the engine for a few seconds on a cold start
issues.sym: A rattle or chain noise from the front of the engine for a few seconds after a cold start, sometimes with timing fault codes later.
issues.why: The timing chain tensioner and the plastic balance shaft sprocket on early versions of the 3.5L V6 can wear early, especially with long oil change intervals.
issues.next: Have a Mercedes specialist check the timing chain and tensioner. Keep up with oil changes using approved synthetic oil.

issues.t: Active Curve System oil can foam and leak (recall)
issues.sym: Oil leaking from the suspension reservoir cap area under the hood.
issues.why: On SUVs with the Active Curve System (active anti-roll bars), low reservoir oil can foam under some driving conditions and push out of the vent holes.
issues.next: Have a dealer check your VIN and inspect the reservoir. The repair is free under the recall.

issues.t: Oil can leak from the timing chain tensioner (recall)
issues.sym: Oil drips or seepage near the front of the engine.
issues.why: The gasket around the chain tensioner on the 2.1L diesel may not seal properly.
issues.next: Have the recall done at a dealer.

issues.t: Emergency call (eCall) system may fail or send the wrong location (recall)
issues.sym: An SOS system warning, or no apparent symptom until the system is needed.
issues.why: Software and SIM card problems in the communication module can stop the automatic crash call from working or make it report the wrong position.
issues.next: Have a dealer check your VIN for open eCall software recalls; the update is free.

issues.t: Engine can shut off when stopping (recall)
issues.sym: The engine shuts down while braking to a stop or pulling away after an automatic stop-start, which can feel like a normal ECO stop.
issues.why: A software conflict between the engine and transmission computers on AMG GLE43 and GLE450 models.
issues.next: Have the free software update done. If the engine stalls, keep firm pressure on the brake and restart.

issues.t: Front roof panel may not be bonded after a sunroof repair (recall)
issues.sym: Wind noise or a loose-feeling panel at the front of the roof.
issues.why: On panoramic-roof models that had the front roof panel repaired, the panel may not have been bonded correctly and could come off.
issues.next: Have a dealer check your VIN, especially if the roof or sunroof was ever repaired.

issues.t: 48-volt ground connection under the passenger seat can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell from under the front passenger seat or 48-volt system warnings.
issues.why: A ground cable bolt for the mild-hybrid 48-volt system may not be tight, causing heat and a fire risk.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 22V-231 and 24V-207. The fix is a quick inspection and retightening.

issues.t: Transmission may not downshift and the engine stalls (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls as you slow down, or downshifts feel rough.
issues.why: The 9-speed automatic may not fully downshift in certain situations, which can stall the GLE450's engine.
issues.next: Get the free transmission software update. If the engine stalls, steering and brakes get heavier, so steer to safety and restart.
issues.eng: 3.0L turbo inline-6 mild hybrid (GLE450, AMG GLE53)

issues.t: Rear driveshaft locking ring may not be connected (recall)
issues.sym: Loss of power to the wheels or the engine stalling.
issues.why: A locking ring between the transfer case and the rear driveshaft may not have been connected correctly.
issues.next: Have the recall checked with your VIN.

issues.t: Rear middle seat belt buckle can slip under the cushion (recall)
issues.sym: The center rear buckle disappears into the gap below the seat and can't be latched.
issues.why: The buckle can be pushed into the gap under the seat cushion.
issues.next: Don't seat anyone in the middle until a dealer fixes it for free.

issues.t: Steering coupling screw can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or looseness in the steering, or steering that doesn't respond normally.
issues.why: The locking screw on the steering coupling may loosen and could detach from the steering gear.
issues.next: Have the free recall repair done promptly. Stop driving if the steering feels loose.

issues.t: Fuel pump can shut down and cut power (recall)
issues.sym: The engine loses power or stalls while driving.
issues.why: The fuel pump may shut down unexpectedly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 23V-445 and 23V-880 and have the free fix done.

issues.t: Front airbag sensor wiring may be routed wrong (recall)
issues.sym: An airbag warning light, or no sign at all.
issues.why: Wiring to a front acceleration sensor may be misrouted, which could keep the front airbags from deploying correctly.
issues.next: Have a dealer inspect and reroute the wiring for free.

issues.t: High-pressure fuel pump may leak fuel and oil (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel or oil smell, or drips under the engine.
issues.why: The wrong screws may have been used on the high-pressure fuel pump, so it doesn't seal against the oil pump and can leak near hot engine parts.
issues.next: Stop driving if you smell fuel and have the recall done right away.

issues.t: Accelerator pedal bracket can break (recall)
issues.sym: The gas pedal feels loose or stops working normally.
issues.why: The bracket that holds the accelerator pedal module may be poorly welded and can break or detach.
issues.next: Have a dealer check your VIN and replace the pedal assembly for free.

issues.t: Windshield camera and mirror can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: The rearview mirror or the camera housing at the top of the windshield is loose or falls off, and driver-assist features may stop working.
issues.why: The mount for the multi-purpose camera and mirror may not be bonded firmly to the windshield.
issues.next: Have a dealer check your VIN and reattach the parts for free.
